_doc: Adversarial premortem P0.2 (2026-09-07): the codeTestable ratings in scripts/nist-800-171/code-testability.json are hand-authored by this project, with zero held-out check before this file existed — the exact gap bench/self-scan/ was built to close for SAST detectors, never extended to compliance labels. This is NOT a full audit of all 97 ratings (that remains a real, disclosed gap — see docs/compliance/nist-800-171-r3-coverage.md). It is a curated set of controls chosen specifically because a reasonable person would not disagree with the expected rating, so this gate exists to catch an ACCIDENTAL drift (a typo, a bad find-and-replace, a careless bulk edit) rather than to validate every judgment call. A mismatch here means something changed that should not have changed silently. Adversarial premortem Q4 (2026-09-07, re-run) found the same author who wrote GOLDEN.json's original 14 anchors had also expanded rationale for 9 controls in the P1.4 second-review pass, but only 3 of those 9 (03.09.01, 03.10.01, 03.15.02) were anchors — the other 6 had NO drift protection despite being the exact work this gate exists to protect. All 9 are now anchors; this set still carries the same self-grading limitation the Q4 finding raised (chosen by the same author, not an independent reviewer) and is disclosed as such, not fixed by adding more of the same author's own judgment.

anchors.why: Weak password hashing (MD5/SHA1) and weak KDFs are directly detected by name; a clean bucket is real evidence.
Weak ciphers, weak hashes, ECB mode are directly detected by name; no organisational judgment required to decide if this fires.
Hardcoded credentials are the single most direct SAST signal this engine produces.
An EOL base image tag (e.g. debian:9, node:12-alpine) is a literal string match, unambiguous.
Finding and fixing flaws is this engine's primary, defining function.
Dependency vulnerability scanning against OSV/KEV is literally what this engine does on every scan.
Personnel background screening happens to a human, off any computer this engine reads.
A locked door and a badge system are physical, never in source code.
Security literacy training is delivered to people in a room or an LMS, never in a repository.
Incident response TRAINING (distinct from the incident response plan artifact) is delivered to people.
Media sanitization before disposal is a physical destruction process.
A System Security Plan is a document authored and reviewed by people, not generated or verified by this engine.
Auth wiring is visible in code; the account-approval workflow around it is a human process this engine cannot see.
Tamper-evident audit-log protection is theoretically code-observable (a detector could exist for it) but this engine has no such detector today — an honest engine gap, not a physical impossibility.

Media storage is a physical fact (a locked room, a controlled cabinet) — nothing about it appears in source code or repository content. Added by adversarial premortem Q4 (2026-09-07): expanded in the same P1.4 rationale pass that added 03.09.01/03.10.01/03.15.02 to this set, but had no drift protection until this entry.
Restricting who may physically handle CUI-bearing media is enforced by locks, custody logs and personnel, not by anything a scanner reads. Added by adversarial premortem Q4 (2026-09-07).
Marking physical media (labels, handling caveats printed on a disk or drive) has no corresponding artifact in source code, configuration, or git. Added by adversarial premortem Q4 (2026-09-07).

Protecting and tracking media in transit outside a controlled area (chain-of-custody logs, courier procedures) is a logistics/physical-security process this engine has no visibility into. Added by adversarial premortem Q4 (2026-09-07).

Monitoring physical access to a facility (camera footage, badge-swipe logs reviewed by security staff) is a physical-security operations activity with no repository artifact. Added by adversarial premortem Q4 (2026-09-07).

Security requirements for alternate work sites (home offices, temporary locations) are administrative/physical controls applied to a workspace, not expressed in source code. Added by adversarial premortem Q4 (2026-09-07).
